title: ‘Adolescence’ Writer Jack Thorne Adapts Matt Haig’s ‘The Humans’ for London’s West End With ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Matt Smith
description: Matt Smith will play an alien inside the body of a Cambridge academic in “The Humans,” a stage adaptation of Matt Haig’s novel by “Adolescence” wri
body:
Matt Smith will play an alien inside the body of a Cambridge academic in “The Humans,” a stage adaptation of Matt Haig’s novel by “Adolescence” writer Jack Thorne. The play will have its world premiere in London’s West End next year.

	Jeremy Herrin (“Wolf Hall,” “People, Places and Things”) will direct the limited run at the Theatre Royal Haymarket. Previews will begin Oct. 30, 2027, opening night is set for Nov. 16, 2027, and the run will close on Jan. 28, 2028. The rest of the cast and the creative team have not yet been revealed.
	

	Smith’s character is never named. He is an extraterrestrial sent to Earth to stop humanity’s progress, which is seen as a threat. He takes over the body of Andrew Martin, a mathematics professor at Cambridge. Living as Martin, he sees humanity at its worst and its best, and he is changed by it.

	Melting Pot and Second Half Productions are producing in association with Access Entertainment, Len Blavatnik and Danny Cohen’s company, which owns the Haymarket. 

	“I love ‘The Humans,’ the chance to work on Matt Haig’s beautiful book with Jeremy Herrin has been an absolute dream. It is a story, at its heart, about an alien learning the complexity of beauty, and I can’t think of a more beautiful alien than Matt Smith,” Thorne said.

	Haig said that “The Humans” may be the most personal of his novels, which makes him protective of it. “I am a massive fan of Jack Thorne and as soon as I saw his incredible script I knew this was being elevated into something very special indeed. And Matt Smith is the absolutely perfect protagonist for this story. He was almost designed for this role. It looks like people will be surprised in all the right ways,” he said.
	

	Herrin said Thorne saw right away what Haig’s story could do on stage, adding that “in Matt Smith we have a beautifully skilled actor of courage and intensity to deliver a performance that will be unforgettable.”

	“I’m thrilled to be reuniting with Jeremy Herrin to bring Matt Haig’s ‘The Humans’ to the stage for the first time, adapted by the brilliant Jack Thorne. It’s going to be a blast,” Smith added.

	Haig’s other novels include “The Midnight Library,” which reached No. 1 on both the Sunday Times and New York Times bestseller lists, and “How to Stop Time.” His nonfiction includes “Reasons to Stay Alive,” and his children’s book “A Boy Called Christmas” was made into a feature film. His work has been translated into more than 50 languages. Thorne’s credits include “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.”

	Herrin founded Second Half in 2020 with Alan Stacey and Rob O’Rahilly. He previously ran Headlong as artistic director and was deputy artistic director of the Royal Court. Melting Pot was launched by Simon Friend in 2015. Its credits include the stage version of “Life of Pi” and the film “The Father,” which won two Oscars.

	Access Entertainment’s film investments include “Conclave” and “The Zone of Interest.” On stage, it has backed Sarah Snook’s “The Picture of Dorian Gray,” as well as the Royal Shakespeare Company’s “Game of Thrones: The Mad King.” That production is due to transfer to London in 2027, the same year Smith, who stars in “House of the Dragon,” takes the Haymarket stage.

title: Taiwan Creative Content Fest Takeaways: ‘Avatar’ VFX House Brings Its AI Ambitions to Taipei as Character IP Booms
description: Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) wrapped its 2026 edition in Taipei with a reshaped show floor, as animation and character IP companies moved to
body:
Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) wrapped its 2026 edition in Taipei with a reshaped show floor, as animation and character IP companies moved to the front of the market.

	They made up the largest exhibitor group, at 29 of 107 exhibitors, up from 19 in 2025, according to post-event figures from organizer the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA). Of this year’s exhibitors, 69 were Taiwanese and 38 came from overseas, compared with 117 exhibitors in total last year.
	

	Elsewhere on the floor, television and media networks rose from 20 to 22 exhibitors, and new media, streaming and entertainment companies from six to eight. Film and TV production and distribution companies dropped from 22 to 16, digital tech, VFX and immersive media from 15 to eight, and publishing, comics and webtoons from 12 to five.

	The Pitching program presented 93 projects and stories, including entries from TAICCA School, to industry participants from 28 countries. TAICCA is still compiling buyer attendance and the value of business done.

	Here are four takeaways from the market:

	Hollywood’s AI Pivot Lands in Taipei

	The headline deal came on opening day, Nov. 6, when Weta FX, the New Zealand visual effects company behind “The Lord of the Rings” and “Avatar,” signed a memorandum of understanding with TAICCA aimed at making Taiwan an AI hub for Asia’s content industries. Weta FX will partner with Taiwanese animation and VFX outfit Moonshine Studio and will set up a technology platform to back Taiwanese film and TV projects, along with exchanges and internships for young Taiwanese filmmakers.
	

	Weta FX CEO Daniel Seah said studio legal departments had ruled out any use of generative AI on their projects early last year. By the turn of the year, clients were asking about Weta’s AI strategy, mostly to find out how much money the technology could save.

	“It’s, ‘If you don’t have an AI strategy, don’t bother to work with us,’” Seah said of the period since the third quarter of this year.

	Seah said AI had become a national strategy in Taiwan on the back of the island’s semiconductor industry, and Moonshine had been moving quickly as a result.

	Japanese studios brought their own AI work to Taipei. Toei, the studio behind “Kamen Rider” and the Super Sentai series that became “Power Rangers,” has adopted rules for generative AI and is already using it for backgrounds, president Yoshimura Fumio said. “I believe AI is not something that takes away jobs, but a tool that expands the possibilities of expression and business,” he said.

	At a TCCF panel on AI in animation, OLM Digital board director Yotsukura Tatsuo presented a coloring tool, developed under a Japanese government-backed research project, that learns a show’s look from three hand-painted frames. On the same panel, Charles Beirnaert, chief creative officer of French studio Blue Spirit, said the “Blue Eye Samurai” studio is barred from using AI on its Netflix work. Taiwanese technology company imCore Corp. launched Core Studio, an AI filmmaking platform with more than 24 specialized agents, at TCCF on Nov. 7.

	Vietnam Rises, Japan Leans In

	“From a television broadcaster’s perspective, we’ve seen a significant increase in Vietnamese buyers this year,” said Grace Chan, a program planner in acquisitions and sales at Taiwan Television Enterprise (TTV). “Last year, Korean buyers and potential partners made up the largest group.”

	Southeast Asia ran through the program. K7 Media’s Trang Nguyen presented a study of Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s biggest film market with box office revenue of $352.9 million in 2025, and pointed to horror as a natural meeting ground for Taiwanese and Indonesian producers. Thai director Thiti Srinuan explained how music video revenue bankrolled much of Taibaan Studio’s film universe before “The Undertaker” grossed more than THB700 million ($20.8 million) in Thailand. The top Pitching prize, the $35,000 TAICCA × CNC Feature Film Grand Award, went to “Somewhere in the South,” a Malaysian feature written and directed by Tan Ce Ding and produced by Anthony Chen, the Singaporean director of “Ilo Ilo.”
	

	Japan was also looking at Taiwan. Cinematographer Wayne Lo, at TCCF for the first time, met several Japanese teams and found that up-and-coming Japanese filmmakers see the market and working directly with TAICCA as routes to getting projects made. “At the pitching sessions, I also sensed growing interest in Taiwanese content in Japan,” Lo said, though he noted that “Japan still offers a wider range of film genres than Taiwan.”

	Toei’s Yoshimura said Japanese films were the most-released titles in Taiwan in 2025 and second only to U.S. films at the box office. He wants long-term tokusatsu partnerships and international co-productions with Taiwan.

	Characters Take Over the Show Floor

	The jump in animation and character IP exhibitors was echoed in the sessions.

	Toei is launching a games label whose first three titles are originals rather than adaptations of its existing IP. “We aim to bring game creators’ talent on board over the long term as a new vein of IP creation, and make games the starting point for stories in place of novels and comics,” Yoshimura said.

	Microdrama producers are thinking the same way. Sawamura Naomichi, founder of Japanese microdrama app Bump, said the company is considering adapting its microdramas into manga or animation.

	Publishing, comics and webtoon exhibitors were down, but books and comics still drew interest through Pitching. Mirror Fiction’s “The Three Witches of Shetou” won both the TAICCA Award: Best Story and the friDay Video Original Story Award. Chang Chen-yu, producer at World Softest Production Film Co., said Taiwanese comic artist Gao Yan’s “The Song About Green” drew considerable attention after its TCCF presentation, and meeting requests were up on last year.

	“Companies from Thailand, South Korea, Singapore and even Europe have expressed interest in collaborating,” Chang said. “This year, I’ve felt more strongly that creative talent and resources are concentrated in Asia, but the distinctiveness and audience appeal of the material remain key.”

	TAICCA’s own audience research backs the push. Among viewers of Taiwanese film and TV, 40% had also watched Taiwanese screen adaptations, and the study flagged romance as a promising genre for cross-platform development, with links to comics, popular music and mobile games.
	

	Telecoms Put Money Into Taiwanese Content

	TAICCA presented the slates of its four joint-venture funds, which have backed 27 projects and drawn NT$4.9 billion in private capital alongside NT$740 million from the agency, about $180 million in all. Two of those ventures are partnerships with Taiwanese telecoms.

	“Beyond OTT [streaming] platforms, the sharp decline in advertising has been the most visible challenge for television stations. Acquisition budgets, meanwhile, have not come down,” TTV’s Chan said. “Through the connections made at the market, we hope to find content that suits our needs and explore original productions and co-productions to diversify risk.”

	The Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative Fund, majority owned by Chunghwa Telecom, totals NT$1 billion ($32 million) and backs both projects and companies. Enjoy Entertainment, TAICCA’s partnership with telecom Far EasTone, invested in 15 projects in its first 10 months. Its slate also includes a Taiwanese remake of Korean series “Our Blues,” which launches globally on Netflix on Dec. 3. The momomini Kids Content Fund focuses on children’s content, which COO Phoebe Tsai said had not previously been treated as a distinct investment category in Taiwan.

	One of Enjoy’s investments ties the week together. “The Rope Curse 4: Kuntilanak,” a Taiwan-Indonesia horror collaboration that Toei also invested in, took NT$80 million ($2.6 million) at the Taiwanese box office, a franchise record.

title: ‘NAZA’ From ‘No Other Land’ Co-Directors Passes 1.5 Million Cinema Admissions Worldwide
description: “NAZA,” the hot-button documentary about killings in Gaza that won a special jury prize at the recent Venice Film Festival, had tallied more than 1
body:
“NAZA,” the hot-button documentary about killings in Gaza that won a special jury prize at the recent Venice Film Festival, had tallied more than 1.5 million theatrical admissions across 47 territories as of Nov. 6. That ranks it among the year’s most-watched documentaries on the big screen.

	The film comes from Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, co-directors of Oscar winner “No Other Land.” It has grossed $13.5 million outside the U.S., with a further $1 million in the U.S.
	

	Italy is the standout. I Wonder opened the doc there on Sept. 29, soon after it debuted in Venice, and it has since drawn 717,517 admissions, nearly half the worldwide total. It is still on 379 screens. “NAZA” has topped the Italian box office and now sits third among documentaries in the country’s cinema history, trailing only “Fahrenheit 9/11” and “March of the Penguins.”

	In the U.S., “NAZA” opened on Sept. 30, self-distributed via Michael Tuckman’s company mTuckman Media. Neon came on board as U.S. distributor in late October, with plans to take the film wider off the back of that first run. Admissions across the U.S. and Canada stand at 83,673.

	Dogwoof opened the film in the U.K. and Ireland on Oct. 15 with an event screening at the Ritz. Abraham and Szor took part in a Q&A alongside producer Jim Wilson and executive producer Jonathan Glazer, and it was beamed live to 104 more cinemas. That night alone sold more than 7,000 tickets. The film went on to play the full Picturehouse circuit, sites from the Odeon, Cineworld and Vue chains, and a handful of independents. Its U.K. and Ireland total now stands at 102,509 admissions.
	

	France took a different route. Local rules on the window before a film can stream online meant “NAZA” played there as a 48-hour event release. Close to 500 screenings in more than 260 theaters drew over 82,000 admissions, and the doc topped the box office on each of the two days.

	Distributor ImmerGuteFilme reported 83,355 admissions in Germany, with the film’s best day so far falling on Sunday, Nov. 1. In Austria, where Polyfilm opened it on Oct. 1, admissions have passed 16,521. In both markets, “NAZA” is running ahead of where “No Other Land” and Kaouther Ben Hania’s “The Voice of Hind Rajab,” an Oscar nominee, stood at the same point.

	Elastica bowed the film in Spain on Oct. 9 on 105 screens, and it reached 61,783 admissions by Nov. 6. Cherry Pickers has counted 132,323 admissions in Benelux, and Switzerland has passed 50,000. The doc has also found audiences in Australia and New Zealand, Scandinavia, Poland, Romania, Mexico, Japan, Indonesia and Thailand.

	The ticket sales have come alongside a busy awards run. Since Venice, the doc has scooped the audience award at San Sebastián and, this week, the critics prize at the Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival. On Nov. 8, the New York Critics Circle named it best political documentary, having also nominated it for documentary feature and for its directors. “NAZA” is up for best documentary feature at the Gotham Awards and has been shortlisted by DOC NYC and, in the European documentary category, by the European Film Awards.

	With Neon now handling the U.S. release, 379 Italian cinemas are still playing the film in its biggest market.

schema.headline: ‘NAZA’ From ‘No Other Land’ Co-Directors Passes 1.5 Million Cinema Admissions Worldwide

title: ITV’s Sale to Sky ‘Progressing as Planned’ as Broadcaster Cuts Fourth-Quarter Content Spend Amid U.K. Ad Slump
description: U.K. broadcaster ITV‘s CEO Carolyn McCall said the broadcaster’s sale of its Media & Entertainment business to Sky is “progressing as planned,” eve
body:
U.K. broadcaster ITV‘s CEO Carolyn McCall said the broadcaster’s sale of its Media & Entertainment business to Sky is “progressing as planned,” even as weaker advertiser demand forced the U.K. company to cut £25 million ($33.4 million) from its fourth-quarter content spend.

	The deal, which covers ITV’s channels and its ITVX streamer, would leave the company as a standalone global content group built around ITV Studios, the producer of “The Gentlemen” and “Line of Duty.” Comcast-owned Sky agreed in July to pay £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) for the business, and ITV still expects it to close in the second half of 2027. On Nov. 4, U.K. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy issued a Public Interest Intervention Notice on the takeover, as Variety reported, opening the way for the Competition and Markets Authority and media regulator Ofcom to examine it and report back to her.
	

	“This is an expected and important milestone in the regulatory review process, and we are pleased that it is moving at pace,” McCall said.

	The business ITV is selling is also the one under pressure. The company now expects total advertising revenue to drop by around 5%–10% in the last three months of 2026 and by roughly 2%–3% across the full year, compared with 2025. ITV will also hold back £5 million ($6.7 million) of discretionary spending outside programming, so the temporary fourth-quarter cuts in Media & Entertainment add up to £30 million ($40 million). Its total 2026 content budget is now projected at about £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion).

	ITV blamed the slowdown on ongoing economic uncertainty, ad money moving toward global streamers and the U.K.’s restrictions on advertising for less healthy food, which kicked in on Oct. 1, 2025. Advertising revenue slipped 1% over the nine months to Sept. 30 and fell 8% in the third quarter alone. The company said it still beat rival broadcasters but missed its earlier guidance.
	

	“Despite a more challenging market, we remain on track to deliver good revenue growth in ITV Studios and continued profitable digital revenue growth in Media & Entertainment (M&E) over the full year,” McCall said.

	Media & Entertainment revenue slid 1% to £1.43 billion ($1.9 billion). Digital revenue rose 7% to £461 million ($615 million), but that wasn’t enough to cover the drop in linear advertising. Hours spent streaming ITV content jumped 29% to 2.15 billion. ITVX set viewing records with the final matches of the soccer World Cup, along with “Trigger Point,” “Big Brother” and “Love Island.” Eight of this year’s 10 most-watched series among commercial broadcasters and streamers have aired on ITV.

	Group revenue dipped 1% to £2.76 billion ($3.7 billion) for the nine-month period. ITV Studios revenue also eased 1%, to £1.33 billion ($1.8 billion). Sales to ITV’s own channels and streamer rose 4% on scripted and unscripted shows, both new and returning, which made up for scheduling changes to the studio’s soap and daytime output. Revenue from outside buyers fell 4%. Distribution income from the studio’s back catalog kept growing.

	McCall said the studio’s nine-month figures matched what the company had expected. “As previously guided, production deliveries and licensing deals are heavily weighted to Q4 this year and despite this, we have a greater proportion of our full year Studios revenue secured than at this point last year,” she said.

	ITV Studios was behind five of the U.K.’s 10 most-watched dramas in the third quarter: “The Gentlemen” for Netflix, “Ludwig” Season 2 and “Vigil” Season 3 for the BBC, and “The Blame” and “The Dark” for ITV. “The Blame” is the most-watched drama of 2026 so far.

	The company still expects the studio to post good full-year revenue growth that outpaces the market. Because of the year’s revenue mix, its EBITA margin should land at the lower end of a 13%–15% range. Fourth-quarter deliveries include “SuburraMaxima” for Netflix, “Love Island US: Beyond the Villa” Season 3 for Peacock, “Hell’s Kitchen” Seasons 25 and 26 for Fox, and “Line of Duty” Season 7, “The Last Detectives” and “The Secret Diary of Adrian Mole Aged 13 ¾” for the BBC. High-margin licensing deals through the Global Partnerships unit will add to the total.
	

	ITV has bought back £81 million ($108 million) of stock so far under its £100 million ($133 million) buyback program.

	“While the outlook for advertising remains muted, we are firmly focused on self help and mitigating actions, while continuing to execute our strategic priorities to drive performance across both businesses,” McCall said.

schema.headline: ITV’s Sale to Sky ‘Progressing as Planned’ as Broadcaster Cuts Fourth-Quarter Content Spend Amid U.K. Ad Slump

title: Netflix’s Genre-Bending YA Drama ‘The Body’ Is a Queer Y2K Extravaganza: TV Review
description: Girlhood is a divine experience, a period when young women begin to discover who they are and who they might become. From “Under the Bridge” creato
body:
Girlhood is a divine experience, a period when young women begin to discover who they are and who they might become. From “Under the Bridge” creator Quinn Shephard, Netflix’s teen drama “The Body” is a twisted coming-of-age narrative that pays homage to the 2000s, specifically films like “Bring It On,” “Jennifer’s Body” and “Mean Girls.” While those movies dealt in subtext, this series is deliciously and unapologetically queer, with one young woman standing firm in who she is while the other is frozen in denial. Set at a Catholic high school somewhere in the Northeast, “The Body” is a raunchy, campy show about friendship, desire, identity and belief systems. 
	

	The eight-episode series opens on Halloween 2004. At St. Barth’s Catholic School, co-captains and best friends Anya Butler (Kristina Bogic) and Elise Zakaria (Sara Boustany), who call each other “wife,” hold emergency tryouts for the school’s all-girls dance troupe the Lions. Star dancer Maddie Delaney (Shirley Chen) has broken her ankle, and with the regional competition two weeks away, the team needs to fill her spot. Among the auditioners are Lisbeth Anderson (Geena Meszaros), who is new in town, and Grace Franklin (Sofia Wylie), the niece of Father Sam Franklin (Nnamdi Asomugha), the head of the school. Grace’s talent clearly surpasses Lisbeth’s.

	Though Lisbeth’s dreams of becoming a Lion are dashed, her spirits lift when Anya, in an attempt at being polite, invites her to a Halloween party at the Devil’s House. In this abandoned convent, the Lions also plan to initiate Grace into the group. Eager to evade her hyper-religious, unwell mother, Catherine (Louisa Krause), Lisbeth urges her brother, Leo (Jackson Kelly), who has his own peculiarities and an obsessive crush on Grace, to cover for her so she can attend the party. 
	

	That night, the soiree spirals out of control. It begins as planned, with all the girls decked out in their provocative Halloween costumes — except Grace, who arrives in a red cape over a nightgown, and Lisbeth, who comes dressed as Jesus in a toga made from bedsheets. Alcohol is flowing, the speakers are bumping and ecstasy is passed around like candy. Grace is initiated as the girls chant, “Prince of Darkness, take this most holy virgin sacrifice, and in exchange let us place at regionals!” But by the time the partygoers awaken the next morning, Grace has been found unresponsive in her bed, and Lisbeth has material she can use to blackmail Anya into friendship. What’s more, the town begins hearing whispers about what befell Grace, which sets off a chain of unsettling events.

	As Father Franklin; Grace’s dad, Michael (Motell Foster); and the rest of the community scramble, the Lions, led by Anya and now Lisbeth — who’s desperate for any sort of respite from her mother’s cult-like beliefs — take a vow of silence about the initiation ritual, erasing any photographic evidence that could link them to the scene. Still, when more than one person knows something, it rarely stays a secret. Soon enough, the Lions, terrorized by guilt and a rocky understanding of Catholicism, begin unraveling.

	“The Body” reflects on how repressive doctrinal religion can be, especially for teens grappling with their identities. After all, oppressive environments often pave the way for shame and inner turmoil, which is one of the central topics of the series. Also, as rumors spread about Grace’s condition, a mass hysteria sweeps through the Lions before spreading across the town. As Father Franklin struggles to figure out what’s happening at his school, he’s confronted by questions he can’t answer while trying to keep confused teenagers from emotionally collapsing.

	Part thriller, part horror and part archetypal YA drama, “The Body” is brilliant. The show treats the Y2K era with the reverence it deserves, and Shephard grounds her audience in the period. “The Body” uses bangers by Chingy, Ciara and Kelly Clarkson; Nokia cellphones with multi-tap texting; and velour tracksuits to depict a time when information moved quickly, but not instantly. And “The Body” shows how, without social media, lies were easier to bury.
	

	With its layered themes, “The Body” stands as a distinct entry among TV’s many teen-oriented offerings. Yet it’s the show’s grasp of the particularities of female friendship, gossip, herd mentality and manipulation (in a very similar vein to religion) that makes it so clever and fun. Lisbeth wants a “normal” teenage experience, and sees Anya as a gateway to that. Elise, who’s in love with Anya, wants to be seen, and Anya wants to maintain her status at all costs. All the girls, lacking impulse control and sensing each other’s unmet needs, use deceit and deviousness to achieve their goals — to varying effect. They make dizzily stupid choices, but their shrewd approaches make for an enthralling watch.

	Taking a page from films like Peter Jackson’s 1994 classic “Heavenly Creatures” and Catherine Hardwicke’s 2003 provocation “Thirteen,” “The Body” is superb because it unpacks the nuances and deep bonds of female friendship, especially as they form and shatter during the teen years. A series about how dazzling and unnerving young women can be, “The Body” is a reminder that the glory of girlhood stems from its intensity.

	“The Body” is now streaming on Netflix.

schema.headline: Netflix’s Genre-Bending YA Drama ‘The Body’ Is a Queer Y2K Extravaganza: TV Review

title: Brenda Song Says She Was ‘Overworked’ and ‘Underpaid’ on ‘The Suite Life of Zack and Cody,’ Recalls Fainting on Set: I Thought, ‘Am I Having a Panic Attack?’
description: Brenda Song recently revealed that she felt she was “overworked” and “underpaid” while starring on “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody.” The “Running
body:
Brenda Song recently revealed that she felt she was “overworked” and “underpaid” while starring on “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody.” The “Running Point” actress opened up about her experience working on the Disney Channel sitcom while appearing on her former co-star Dylan Sprouse’s and co-host Brendan Columbus’ “Wildmen” podcast.

	“I’ve been curious to ask you about this. Like, I feel like there are parts of the ‘Suite Life’ that are, like, black holes for me. Like, I don’t remember years of my life,” Song said, before moving onto the subject of residuals. “I look at that time and I was like, we paid them,” Song said. “I always say this about my time at Disney, is like, I know everybody has their own journey [because]… I always say, like, I have a boring tale… I had a lovely time.”
	

	Song did admit that she passed out on set once while filming a scene that called for a hot tub, which malfunctioned and was heated to “250 degrees,” said Sprouse. “I remember just breathing really heavy, and my chest felt really hot. I just went, ‘Am I having a panic attack?’ And then all of a sudden I remember stars and gone.”

	She continued: “I think the only thing that was hard about that time was I feel like we were underpaid and overworked. But Disney did give us a platform to be sitting here right now. So it’s very hard to complain about certain things.”

	Earlier this month, Sprouse also touched on how the show was “extremely underfunded,” despite being “popular” on his podcast. “In terms of the channel higher-ups, we were also kind of weirdly the ugly duckling,” Sprouse said, before adding that “the only residual check I’ve ever received for ‘The Suite Life’ at all was a crossover episode with ‘Hannah Montana’ for five cents. I’m not joking,” he said. “Imagine that. In a time where residuals would have been great,” Sprouse added, “Not a single paycheck for being arguably one of the most popular shows.”
	

	The “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody” ran from 2005 to 2008 and followed the titular Zack and Cody as they lived at the Tipton Hotel with their single mother. Song played teenage heiress London Tipton. The show inspired a spinoff, “The Suite Life on Deck,” which aired from 2008 to 2011. Song, Debby Ryan, Erin Cardillo and more starred in the continuation.

schema.headline: Brenda Song Says She Was ‘Overworked’ and ‘Underpaid’ on ‘The Suite Life of Zack and Cody,’ Recalls Fainting on Set: I Thought, ‘Am I Having a Panic Attack?’

title: Jamie Dornan Admits He ‘Cried’ When He Was Cast as Aragorn in ‘Lord of the Rings: Hunt for Gollum’ and Says Filming Was ‘Incredible’: ‘Hopefully We’ve Done a Good Job’
description: Jamie Dornan, who is set to star as Aragorn in “Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum,” is getting candid about what it means to step into the rol
body:
Jamie Dornan, who is set to star as Aragorn in “Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum,” is getting candid about what it means to step into the role originated by Viggo Mortensen for the forthcoming installment of the beloved franchise.

	“I cried. I actually cried,” Dornan told Entertainment Tonight when asked how he reacted to the news of his casting. “It’s like a dream. It’s an absolute dream and an honor to be entering that world in any capacity, let alone playing a character of such significance and such admiration, and that we all love and love what Viggo did with that role in those three films.”
	

	He continued, noting that filming “The Hunt for Gollum” was “incredible.” “[I’m] incredibly honored and had a brilliant time. I finished like three weeks ago. It was an incredible experience, and I hope people welcome our story into that world because a lot of people care about it, and I really realize that. But yeah, hopefully we’ve done a good job of it.”

	Last month, Dornan admitted during an interview with L’Officiel that while there is “pressure” on him to live up to Mortensen’s take on the character, there’s no part of him that is “trying to outdo him.” “I’ve been asked to play a super iconic role, and I’ll do my best. But for me, Aragorn will always be just Viggo. His performance is one of my all-time favorites, and I feel honored to try to recapture at least some of the energy he originally brought to the character,” he said.

	Andy Serkis, who provided the voice and motion capture for the CGI hobbit in Peter Jackson’s original trilogy, directed the film, which is set to open in theaters Dec. 17, 2027. The ensemble also sees the return of Ian McKellen (as Gandalf), Elijah Wood (Frodo) and Lee Pace (King Thranduil), in addition to new cast members Kate Winslet (Marigol), Leo Woodall (Halvard) and Anya Taylor-Joy as an elf.

schema.headline: Jamie Dornan Admits He ‘Cried’ When He Was Cast as Aragorn in ‘Lord of the Rings: Hunt for Gollum’ and Says Filming Was ‘Incredible’: ‘Hopefully We’ve Done a Good Job’

title: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to Headline Coachella 2027
description:
Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA are set to headline Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival 2027.

	News of the lineup comes after SZA teased the he
body:
Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA are set to headline Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival 2027.

	News of the lineup comes after SZA teased the headliners on social media. Daddy Yankee has his own special slot, typically reserved as a bonus fourth headliner, as does Justice, who will have the Bunker debut of “Blinded by the Lights.” Additional artists who have top billing include Madonna, who is returning to the Dance Tent as she did when she released “Confessions on a Dance Floor” back in 2006. Phoebe Bridgers, Don Toliver, Zara Larsson, Weezer, Dom Dolla, Kygo, Empire of the Sun and Role Model also dot the upper tiers. 
	

	Further down the listing are Kehlani, Jisoo, Tiesto, Adéla, Maneskin, Four Tet, Becky G, the Neighbourhood, Remi Wolf, Victoria Monét, Caroline Polachek, EsDeeKid, Underworld, Nettspend, Pinegrove, Leon Thomas, Peggy Gou, Giorgio Moroder, Mariah the Scientist, Babymonster, Magdalena Bay, Murda Beatz, Xaviersobased, Bella Kay, Haute & Freddy, Bea Miller, Gang of Youths, Martin Garrix and many more.

	Coachella 2027 will take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California, for two weekends set for April 9-11 and April 16-18. Passes go on sale starting on November 13 at 12 p.m. PT on the festival’s website.

	YouTube will once again return for its 15th year as the exclusive livestream partner for those who are unable to attend. Hotel packages bundling passes with lodging and transportation are now available for both weekends.

	The lineup comes after a standout year for Coachella, which included headlining sets from Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber, Karol G and Anyma. Madonna, who is billed high on the list for this year, came out as a surprise guest during weekend two of Carpenter’s set to debut their single “Bring Your Love.”

title: MCU Surprise: ‘VisionQuest’ Finale Teases the Return of [SPOILER] in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains major spoilers for “Forever,” the finale of “VisionQuest,” now streaming on Disney+.

	The “WandaVision” Saga ha
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains major spoilers for “Forever,” the finale of “VisionQuest,” now streaming on Disney+.

	The “WandaVision” Saga has come to a close with the final episode of the Disney+ series “VisionQuest.” But it seems as though the story of the ultra-powerful Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen), the synthezoid Vision (Paul Bettany) and their super-powered children will continue in the MCU.


	The season finale sees Vision reunite with his and Wanda Maximoff’s grown-up sons, Ruaridh Mollica’s Tommy Maximoff (who was key to “VisionQuest”) and Joe Locke’s Billy Maximoff (whose eleventh-hour arrival completes the family reunion). Then, the post-credit scene replays the ending of 2022’s feature film “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” where Wanda eradicated the Darkhold from all of the multiverse before (seemingly) being crushed from within a mountain.
	

	However, this time, the scene continues with the appearance of Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom, who lifts the rubble off Wanda and addresses her. 

	“Scarlet Witch, awaken — your power will be mine,” Doom says, as Wanda gasps and opens her eyes.

	The coda confirms fan speculation that Wanda would return as the Avengers face off against Doom in “Avengers: Doomsday,” out Dec. 18. And she’s not the only powerful hero that Doom has now rounded up. In “Avengers Endgame: Encore,” Doom kidnapped the Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) in a newly added post-credits scene.

	Ahead of the finale, Marvel tweeted a message written in binary code, which fans were quick to decode as a quote from “WandaVision.” Though the tweet was written with a series of 0s and 1s, it translated to: “We could never truly leave each other, even if we tried.” The line is from the show’s 2021 finale.
	

01010111 01100101 00100000 01100011 01101111 01110101 01101100 01100100 00100000 01101110 01100101 01110110 01100101 01110010 00100000 01110100 01110010 01110101 01101100 01111001 00100000 01101100 01100101 01100001 01110110 01100101 00100000 01100101 01100001 01100011 01101000…— Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) November 10, 2026


	Olsen first appeared as Wanda in the post-credits scene for 2014’s “Captain America: The Winter Soldier,” which set up her full-fledged debut in 2015’s “Avengers: Age of Ultron.” Despite her wide-ranging powers of telekinesis and mind manipulation, Wanda’s first forays in the MCU were laden with tragedy, including the death of her brother Pietro (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), the devastation of her home country of Sokovia in “Age of Ultron,” and then the death of her beloved Vision (Paul Bettany) in 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War.”

	That trauma led to 2021’s “WandaVision,” Marvel Studios‘ first TV series for Disney+, in which Wanda’s overwhelming grief led her to take over an entire New Jersey town and transform it into a recreation of American sitcoms — complete with a reconstituted Vision and two twin sons, Billy and Tommy. By the end of the series, she had to let go of Vision and her sons, all while her interactions with the witch Agatha Harkness (Kathryn Hahn) revealed Wanda to be the Scarlet Witch, one of the most powerful beings in the Marvel universe. Agatha’s witchy, post-“WandaVision” escapades continued in the 2024 Disney+ series “Agatha All Along,” which introduced Joe Locke as Wanda and Vision’s grown-up son Billy Maximoff. 

	Wanda’s story continued in 2022’s “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” in which her grief from the loss of her children led her to turn fully evil as the film’s central villain. She brutally killed anyone standing in opposition to her desire to find her boys within the multiverse, fueled by the corrupting book of magic, the Darkhold. By the end, Wanda understood all the harm she had caused, and she eradicated the Darkhold from all of the multiverse before (seemingly) being crushed from within Wundagore mountain.

	When asked by Variety in 2022 whether she hoped to play Wanda again, however, Olsen sounded optimistic.

	“It’s weird that I’m expecting to return, but no one’s told me I’m doing anything!” she said with a laugh. “But in my mind, I’m just making the assumption that they’ll have me again. I don’t know to what capacity, but I hope I’m back. I hope there’s also more fun to be had in something different.”

title: Brandy and Monica Announce ‘The Boy Is Mine’ 2027 Residency at Las Vegas’ Resorts World
description:
Brandy and Monica have announced “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency,” their first-ever series of shows in Las Vegas.

	The R&B icons announced the re
body:
Brandy and Monica have announced “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency,” their first-ever series of shows in Las Vegas.

	The R&B icons announced the residency following a performance of their collaborative hit “The Boy Is Mine” on “Dancing With the Stars” during its Grammy-themed episode on Tuesday night. The 10-date residency will take place at Resorts World Las Vegas, kicking off on May 29 with performances through June before concluding on July 17.
	

	Produced by the Black Promoters Collective, the residency comes following their sold-out “The Boy Is Mine” tour, which saw each artist trading off to perform hits and deep cuts from their respective catalogs. Following the conclusion of the tour in December 2025, Brandy and Monica continued to perform together at the St. Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival and a co-headlining performance at the 2026 Essence Festival of Culture. Read Variety‘s review of Brandy and Monica’s Los Angeles tour stop here.

	In a statement shared with Variety, Monica says that she did not initially envision the tour extending to a residency. “Originally, it was planned as a one and done, but I’ll be honest, after the first night, I realized it was far deeper,” she said, touching on the key to her working relationship with Brandy. “I think the most important factor in any relationship or friendship, especially one that has a partnership like ours, is communication. Communication is key, and keeping other people out, allowing us to speak about the things that matter, to talk about things when one may like something or may not like something, making sure other people’s feelings don’t become our own. [It’s] the key component to how we make sure things work best.”
	

	“BPC is proud to be working with Brandy and Monica again,” says Shelby Joyner, President of Black Promoters Collective, in a statement. “We saw on The Boy Is Mine tour how much it meant to fans to see them share a stage, and I’m excited to build on what we created together. Bringing The Boy Is Mine to Las Vegas as Black Promoters Collective’s first residency is a big moment for us. We’ve built BPC by betting on artists we believe in and listening to their fans. This residency takes that work into a new arena for our company, and I can’t think of two artists I’d rather take that step with.”

	American Express presale begins on November 11 at 10 a.m. PT, followed by artist presale at 12 p.m. PT. Local presales start on November 12 at 10 a.m. PT, and general onsale kicks off on November 20 at 10 a.m. PT.

	Check out “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency” dates below:

	Saturday, May 29 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSunday, May 30 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasWednesday, June 2 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasFriday, June 4 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSaturday, June 5 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasFriday, July 9 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSaturday, July 10 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasWednesday, July 14 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasFriday, July 16 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSaturday, July 17 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las Vegas



	

	



	With additional reporting from Tim Chan

title: Turning Point USA Denies Involvement in Alleged Rutgers University Assault
description:
Turning Point USA
                          Fires Back at Student Assault Allegation
body:
Turning Point USA
                          Fires Back at Student Assault Allegation
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 10, 2026
                            7:25 PM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 10, 2026
                                7:57 PM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A woman who claims to be a former volunteer Rutgers University student chapter Vice President of Turning Point USA says she was assaulted at one of their events in Maryland, however Turning Point denies their employees knew of the situation or were involved ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            The woman said in video shared to social media that earlier this year she attended a social event where several male members had "assaulted and violated" her. She reported the incidence to local police, but there is no word on the status of their investigation.
      
    
            A Turning Point legal representative tells TMZ ... the organization "takes assault allegations incredibly seriously" and they have a rigorous response process.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The rep continues ... "When we were notified of the incident in October, more than 3 months after the July event in question, we immediately launched an internal investigation and attempted to interview all those involved. While multiple people in the room or with knowledge of the incident provided statements, videos, and text messages, [accusers name] declined to participate on four different occasions."
      

            We're told by the organization ... "The room in which the alleged incident occurred was not part of the Turning Point USA room block" and that "individuals independently booked that room."
      
    
            The organization tells us everyone who was interviewed "were adamant that no sexual assault occurred." Turning Point tells TMZ the blood on [her] clothing was from her period, not a result of any assault, according to people who were there.
      
    
            The rep says "The Rutgers PD report that was eventually filed on October 26th also doesn't include any allegations of sexual assault, but instead references video 'that appears to depict consensual face-slapping with [the accuser] slapping an unidentified male and pillow fighting.'"
      
    
            The organization tells TMZ ... "The male student involved in the alleged incident was removed from the event the next day following an unrelated matter, after which he was immediately disinvited from future events and has no affiliation with the organization."
      
    
            The rep is adamant "At no point were any TPUSA staff involved, nor was staff made aware of these allegations during the event. Had they been brought to our attention, we would have immediately assisted the student in engaging law enforcement and provided all necessary support. Student safety remains our top priority."
